title: Alan Dawson and finding successors to teach
summary: Hinton credits Alan Dawson with teaching Jones's sock cymbal and brush work; Jones recalls meeting him in Boston and sending him to a teacher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: You know I've been teaching in a couple of music schools in a couple of places. I taught a course up at the University of Maryland and a very great young drummer, modern drummer today that loved you dearly and speaks so highly of you is Aldn Dawson. He taught a course up there showing young drummers the procedure and where it came from. He gave you so much credit for the sock cymbal and the great brush work that you did, that nobody was doing before you. You know of Aldn Dawson, do you?
He's one of the great young ones, don't you think?

Yes, because at the particular time when Sid Catlett and I - I replaced Sid Catlett in Boston to play George Wein's Storyville. When we looked at Aldan - 'cause we always tried to find a replacement for us, all throughout the United States. As you know, you had a little cousin that I tried to do something. He played with Lester Young. O.K.?
Right, Wendell. Now these are our children.

So now we come in the world with nothing; we go out with nothing. Wherever we could catch kids, instead of having a quart of whiskey on one arm and a chick on the other, we went and got these peoples and said, "Come on, it's out here." We couldn't play all 48 states. I said, "Alon, who are you studying with?" He had so many knots in his string we didn't know where to start, so we sent him to Mr. Gardner instead of George Stone. He has worked that thing out so marvelous to the fact that he can be an instructor and still can play, six of one and a half a dozen of the other. It's very difficult to do because a lot of us have a flair to instruct, which you instruct drums. But I had told him, "We won't want any dumb drummers. You will be playing vibraphones, chimes, and tymps. You will be known as a musician. Your instrument is drums."
